{{Short description|Concept in mathematics}}
{{no footnotes|date=September 2025}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''tensor bundle''' of a [[manifold]] is the [[Direct sum of vector bundles|direct sum]] of all tensor products of the [[tangent bundle]] and the [[cotangent bundle]] of that manifold. To do [[calculus]] on the tensor bundle a [[Connection (mathematics)|connection]] is needed, except for the special case of the [[exterior derivative]] of antisymmetric tensors.

==Definition==
{{See also|Tensor field#Tensor bundles|Tensor product bundle}}

A tensor bundle is a [[fiber bundle]] where the fiber is a tensor product of any number of copies of the [[tangent space]] and/or [[cotangent space]] of the base space, which is a manifold. As such, the fiber is a [[vector space]] and the tensor bundle is a special kind of [[vector bundle]]. Explicitly, for fixed non-negative integers <math>p</math> and <math>q</math>, a tensor bundle is the fiber bundle
: <math>V \otimes \cdots \otimes V \otimes V^* \otimes  \cdots  \otimes V^* = V^{\otimes p}\otimes (V^*)^{\otimes q}</math>
where ''V'' is the [[tangent bundle]] of ''M'' and ''V''<sup>∗</sup> is the [[cotangent bundle]] of ''M'', and its fibers are
: <math>V_x \otimes \cdots \otimes V_x \otimes V_x^* \otimes  \cdots  \otimes V_x^* = V_x^{\otimes p}\otimes (V_x^*)^{\otimes q}</math>
where <math>V_x</math> is the tangent space of ''x'' and <math>V_x^*</math> is the cotangent space of ''x'', for every ''x'' in ''M''. The elements of the fibers are tensors of type <math>(p,q) \in \N\times\N</math>.

The direct sum of vector bundles allows to consider all these posibilities of tensor bundle for fixed <math>(p,q)</math> as a single mathematical object<math display="block"> \bigoplus_{(p,q) \in \N\times\N} V^{\otimes p}\otimes (V^*)^{\otimes q}.</math>
